articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Partial Discharge in Single Core Power Cables
publicationTitle: 2022 Third International Conference on Intelligent Computing Instrumentation and Control Technologies (ICICICT)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) is a phenomenon of electrical discharge between two adjacent conductors. Analysis of PD plays a major role in condition monitoring and of power cable. In this paper, modeling, and analysis of partial discharge (PD) in a single core power cable is presented. Examination of a single-core fault occurring is examined when it is particularly subjected to the partial discharge activities. A detailed study in relation to the effect of void in the solid dielectric of such cable, as well as the supply voltage, is carried out using EMTP-RV. The studies are conducted under different conditions, the results and presented and discussed.

articleTitle: An Efficient Scheme for Facial Expression Recognition using Random Forest and CNN
publicationTitle: 2022 Third International Conference on Intelligent Computing Instrumentation and Control Technologies (ICICICT)
abstract: As humans, we use our facial expressions to communicate our thoughts and feelings without saying a word. The recognition of these facial expressions can provide a better idea of people’s thoughts or opinions. At present, the high performance of deep learning procedures has influenced the high efficiency of image recognition systems. This paper proposes a Facial Expression Recognition System (FER) using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). We have made use of features such as Gabor wave coefficients, Histogram of Oriented Gradient (HOG), Speed-Up Robust Features (SURF), and Local Binary Patterns (LBP). We have used the Random Forest algorithm for the selection of the best features from the extracted feature set, accordingly, the learning procedure can be faster. The widely used CK+ database can be used for the appraisal of our proposed system. We have also compared our proposed method against similar FER systems and the consequences are satisfactory.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection System Using Computationally Efficient SVM based on K-Prototype Clustering
publicationTitle: 2022 Third International Conference on Intelligent Computing Instrumentation and Control Technologies (ICICICT)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are crucial to the safety of a network because it allows the IT personnel to be warned about suspicious activity and malicious attacks. Over the years, there has been a lot of improvement in IDS technology using Machine Learning Techniques. In this paper, we propose a new hybrid ML model for IDS using K-prototype clustering and Support Vector Machines (SVM). Support vector machines being a large margin classifier is very efficient in terms of accuracy for classification problems. However, when the training data is large, it can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. In this aspect, there is scope for improvement using the K-prototype model. The original KDD-1999 data set consists of 4.9 million rows and 43 columns. Training an unmodified SVM model on the entire data set can be very costly in terms of the number of computations and time taken to train the model. We designed a model that effectively chooses the most important samples of data for training SVM without compromising the model in terms of accuracy using a combination of K-Prototype and SVM. The proposed model reduces the number of training samples, which in turn reduces the number of support vectors thereby reducing the time taken to train SVM while still producing impressive results.

articleTitle: MMD labeling in the context of larger families of bipartite graphs
publicationTitle: 2022 Third International Conference on Intelligent Computing Instrumentation and Control Technologies (ICICICT)
abstract: Let the graph G has r vertices and let g be a relation from the vertex set of G to {1,2,…,r} such that each vertex takes exactly one value i, 1 ≤ i ≤ r which is both one to one and onto. Let g* be a function induces edge labeling from the edge set of G to {0,1,…r-1}defined as g*(wv)=g(w)g(v)(mod r), for every edge vw in G . Collecting all edge labels and finding their addition if it is the divisor of r then the graph G is a modular multiplicative divisor (MMD) graph. Here discuss an arbitrary super subdivision of MMD bipartite graphs.
